analysis.title: Weekly Economic Roundup (26 October 2026)
key_insights: PNC expects the FOMC to keep the federal funds rate unchanged at this week's meeting. Fed officials have aligned around a patient, slower approach to further rate hikes, and the recent AI-driven selloff in equities and bonds gives policymakers additional cover to wait despite hotter September inflation readings.

Fed communication in recent weeks points to three things: inflation is still too high, the Fed will need to hike more, and policymakers should be patient with the cadence of hikes. PNC calls the likely outcome a hawkish hold.
September inflation readings were hot and broad-based, so the hold does not reflect improved inflation.

The risk balance around hiking differs from 2022. The economy then added about 500,000 jobs a month with two vacancies per unemployed person. It now adds about 50,000 jobs a month, and there is little room to reduce labor demand without raising unemployment.
PNC expects minimal changes to the FOMC statement and little explicit forward guidance from Chairman Warsh's press conference.

The key signal from the meeting is whether there are dissents in favor of a hike. PNC thinks a dissent is very likely from Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, and whether other officials join her is the most informative element.

Q3 real GDP, out Thursday, is expected to show growth accelerating to an above-3% pace (PNC 3.1%, consensus 3.2%, prior 2.2%). Strong consumer spending and an AI-related capex boom are keeping demand strong.

September personal income and spending, out Thursday, is expected to show some loss of consumer momentum. Real spending is seen up just 0.1% m/m, while nominal spending rises 0.5% (partly reflecting higher gas prices) and core PCE stays elevated at 0.3% m/m.

The Employment Cost Index, out Friday, should give a cleaner read on wage pressure than average hourly earnings, which have steadily weakened this year. ECI controls for occupation and industry, so it removes compositional effects from the mix of job growth.
The week's data should show solid growth with slowing consumer momentum and inflation that remains too high. That supports the Fed staying patient without closing the door on more hikes.

risk_factors: Inflation remains too high and broad-based, and the Fed may need to hike further.
Little room to reduce labor demand without a rise in unemployment, with job growth at about 50,000 a month.
Consumer momentum is slowing, with real spending growth weak and higher gas prices, weaker real income growth, higher rates and affordability challenges weighing on households.
Hawkish dissents could signal the committee is moving toward a hike sooner than PNC expects.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish officials such as Beth Hammack favor smaller, quicker adjustments rather than waiting and risking a larger correction, and September inflation was hot and broad-based.
tension_points.bear_case: Job growth is only about 50,000 a month with little room to cut labor demand without raising unemployment, and the AI-driven selloff in equities and bonds gives the Fed cover to wait.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Dissents in favor of a hike beyond Hammack at this week's FOMC meeting would signal a faster hiking path than the patient approach PNC expects.

theme_stances.key_argument: The Fed is right to be patient and monitor how the labor market responds to additional rate hikes.
theme_stances.evidence: the Fed is right, in our view, to be patient
